subject: Post-call: deployment path & latency profile — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@fastmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: deployment path & latency profile — next steps

Hi Emilia / Tom —

Great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can align the right deployment path (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private). Key notes from the call: 

- Current feature: on-page product recommendations (real-time) + cart personalization.
- Expected peak: ~1,200 qps for inference during sales peaks (2–3 hour windows), baseline steady-state ~180 qps.
- Latency target: 95th <= 120ms end-to-end for single-token generation in production; tail matters for checkout flows.
- Data concerns: product catalog & user IDs are not regulated but you want data-segregation options.

What we need from you to make a recommendation:
1) Confirmation of true peak QPS and average request size (tokens in prompt + response).
2) Whether you can tolerate latency variability (e.g., occasional 300–400ms during peaks) or if strict tail SLO is required for checkout.
3) Any compliance constraints that would push you to Private (VPC/on-prem) beyond data segregation preference.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Fast pilot on Hosted API to validate accuracy and latency at baseline (we can do a 2-week hosted pilot).
- If tail latency needs strict control on high peaks, we recommend exploring Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools and autoscaling.
- I'll loop Neha to run a quick throughput/latency estimate given your token sizes and QPS.

Attachments: I attached the draft SOW and a quick template pilot offer.

Suggested calendar: 30-min technical follow-up next Tue to confirm inputs and pilot sizing.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path & latency profile — next steps

Thanks Sean —

A few clarifications from our side after chatting with engineering: 
- Peak is more like 1,400 qps if we include headless checkout spikes; average 220 qps.
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens; typical response: 40 tokens. So ~160 tokens round-trip on average.
- For checkout we need 95th <= 150ms ideally; marketing widgets can tolerate 400ms.
- We prefer data isolation for product catalogs but we do NOT require on-prem. VPC/private endpoint would be a nice-to-have.

Tom raised a question: at 1,400 qps with the 160 token size, does Hosted API economically make sense or should we go straight to Dedicated? Also curious about how caching/prefixing would change the requirement.

Can we do the technical follow-up Wednesday morning PST?

—Emilia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@fastmart.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: deployment path & latency profile — next steps

Hi Emilia — thanks for the details, super helpful.

Quick read: based on ~1,400 qps with 160 tokens, two paths make sense: 

Option A — Hosted API pilot (recommended to start):
- Pros: Lowest time-to-live, we provision pilotscale throughput on hosted with caching and request shaping. Cost-effective for validation, easy rollback.
- Cons: Tail latency during sustained spikes may be higher; we'll provide an SLO-aware routing policy and burst protection.
- Offer: 2-week hosted pilot with a throughput band up to 1,500 qps for peak windows; support credit if we miss agreed latency windows during pilot.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended for long term if tail matters):
- Pros: Predictable tail, dedicated GPU pools, configurable autoscale and burst buffers, better isolation (not tenant-level private but reserved).
- Cons: Commitment, longer provisioning lead time (2–4 weeks).

We can layer a VPC/private control-plane later if you decide to move to Private — that’s a separate packaging step.

Neha — can you run a quick back-of-envelope on estimated instance counts and expected 95th latency if we target 1,400 qps and use our standard radix-quant (int8) profile? Please include caching assumptions (25% prefix reuse) and batching window 8–12ms.

Emilia — if you’re OK, I’ll send an updated pilot SOW (short) and we’ll lock a Wednesday morning slot for the tech deep-dive.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
